headline: Israeli Shekel Slips to 14-Month Low Against US Dollar Amid Political and Market Pressures
summary: The Israeli shekel weakened to its lowest level in 14 months against the US dollar, pressured by Wall Street losses, global dollar strength, and domestic geopolitical uncertainties.
why: Currency exchange rates reflect international confidence in a country's economic stability, foreign capital flows, and geopolitical risk profile.

impacts.name: Israeli shekel
impacts.why: Geopolitical uncertainty and domestic risk premiums cause foreign investors to sell local currency.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Domestic political instability, regional geopolitical friction, and a globally stronger dollar triggered capital outflows from Israeli assets.
